skill: Integrate a three-term sum of power functions using radical/reciprocal-to-power rewriting, linearity, and the power rule.
learner_operation: For each term identify its signed coefficient and rational exponent, increase the exponent by one and divide by that new exponent, then select the complete antiderivative with one arbitrary constant.
reasoning_steps: Rewrite radicals and reciprocals as rational powers.
Separate the sum and take signed constant factors outside.
Apply integral x^p dx = x^(p+1)/(p+1), p != -1, to every term.
Simplify powers/coefficient fractions and combine with +C; compare all answer terms.

Moderate evidence includes three-term polynomials and binomial-square expansion. Untagged q-29830 has a high polynomial power and both root and reciprocal-root terms.
